name: U.S.-Iran Conflict / Strait of Hormuz
status: IRGC bundles 8-9 Sep destroyer claims (naming USS Delbert D. Black DDG-119 and USS John Paul Jones DDG-53) with a real 31 Aug ballistic-missile strike on Jordan's Muwaffaq Salti/Al-Azraq air base under a named operation, 'Ya Haidar Karrar'; CENTCOM again calls the destroyer claim 'completely FALSE' and reports destroying 5 more Iranian tankers (~10 total in the past week) as part of a 'shadow network.' Brent crude closed at $101.21/bbl (9 Sep, +3.4%). A specialist tracker (war-risk-insurance-based) describes Hormuz as effectively closed for 192 days; this conflicts with the ~10 ships/day figure from shipping-data aggregators cited in the prior cycle — the discrepancy is unresolved.
importance: Critical — the sharpest escalation of the reignited U.S.-Iran conflict to date, now including a consolidated Iranian narrative pairing a real land-strike precedent with contested naval claims, alongside deepening tanker attrition and a genuine open-source data gap on actual strait openness.
assessment: Two-track escalation continues and is now more structured: Iran is bundling a real (if intercepted) strike on a US-linked allied air base with unconfirmed naval claims under one operation name, sustaining an escalation narrative even as CENTCOM's tanker-attrition campaign imposes rising, quantifiable costs. Miscalculation risk remains materially elevated. Separately, the Hormuz-openness data gap between two credible source types (insurance-based vs. shipping-data-based) is itself now a standing planning risk.
lastChange: 2026-09-10 — IRGC names destroyers (DDG-119, DDG-53) and frames claims under operation 'Ya Haidar Karrar,' explicitly linking the 31 Aug Jordan air-base strike; CENTCOM denies again; tanker toll reaches ~10 destroyed in the past week; Brent hits $101.21; a specialist tracker's 'effectively closed' framing surfaces as conflicting with the previously-cited ~10 ships/day transit figure.
orgRelevance: Reassess Hormuz-transit shipping, insurance, personnel, and supply-chain exposure now; reconcile the two competing transit-openness data sets before briefing a single figure to leadership, and plan against the more conservative reading in the interim.
nextIndicator: Independent (non-Iranian, non-U.S.) confirmation or refutation of the 8-9 Sep strike claims; any further attempted strike on a U.S. or allied vessel; reconciliation of the conflicting Hormuz transit-volume data; tanker-attrition rate and Brent/insurance trajectory.

name: Critical Minerals / Rare-Earth Magnets
status: China's military-affiliated license-denial rule (since 1 Dec 2025) and the June 2026 entity-list targeting of MP Materials/USA Rare Earth remain the binding constraints; no new PRC action confirmed this cycle. The broader Oct 2025 rare-earth controls remain suspended until their 10 Nov 2026 expiry, now roughly two months out.
importance: Critical — binding, targeted constraint on munitions/platform output and the domestic-substitution response itself, now compounded by active Hormuz-theater munitions consumption and a newly surfaced Navy-shipbuilding demand vector.
assessment: Durable, weaponizable chokepoint at its already-escalated severity; no signal of near-term relaxation ahead of the 10 Nov suspension-expiry decision or the 24 Sep Trump-Xi summit. Structural risk remains HIGH; near-term program impact MODERATE-to-HIGH given entity-list targeting, rising Hormuz-theater munitions consumption, and now a third demand vector from the CVN-81 steam-catapult/elevator redesign.
lastChange: 2026-09-10 — no new PRC action this cycle; continuity at the escalated severity. Noted that a separate BIS 'Affiliates Rule' export-control suspension is also keyed to a 10 Nov 2026 date, an incidental regulatory-calendar convergence with the rare-earth suspension expiry worth tracking.
orgRelevance: Map magnet exposure in hardware BOMs against named entities; pursue second sources, including newer SRM/munitions entrants (Anduril, Ursa Major, X-Bow) and any carrier-catapult/elevator-adjacent suppliers, outside China-targeted firms.
nextIndicator: DoD mine-to-magnet award cadence and FORGE-initiative disbursement; any further PRC entity-list or licensing action; the 10 Nov 2026 suspension-expiry decision; rare-earth movement at or around the 24 Sep Trump-Xi summit.

The MikroTik 'MikroTrick' chain remains unlisted eight days after its detailed IOC was published.
importance: High — trust-boundary, perimeter/authentication, endpoint, and MSP/RMM-supply-chain components common in enterprise and DIB networks, now spanning five distinct vendor families in under three weeks.
assessment: The cohort widened again this cycle: Citrix NetScaler and Cisco Firewall Management Center — both authentication/policy control-plane devices — joined KEV alongside a Fortinet heap overflow and another Chromium flaw, on top of the still-unlisted MikroTik chain. The density and vendor spread (five families in under three weeks) is unusual and indicates broad, opportunistic targeting of perimeter infrastructure.

name: Ukraine Ceasefire Diplomacy / Zaporizhzhia
status: The 3-day Kyiv-Moscow capital-strike pause (tied to the Witkoff/Kushner envoy visit) lapsed on schedule 8 Sep with a mass Russian attack on Kyiv (166 drones, 32 cruise missiles, ballistic/anti-ship missiles) killing several and injuring dozens; NATO Sec-Gen Rutte says Ukrainian civilian deaths are at their highest level since May 2022. A separate, narrower 30-day energy-infrastructure-specific halt commitment from the 7 Sep Trump-Putin call remains unconfirmed as violated. ZNPP remains on restored external power (since 7 Sep).
importance: High — shapes European security and munitions/air-defense demand; the ZNPP dimension carries independent nuclear-safety significance.
assessment: The capital-strike pause's clean lapse (with a heavy resumed attack) confirms the base-case forecast from two cycles ago. The separate energy-infrastructure-specific halt's status is genuinely unresolved rather than disproven, since the 8 Sep targets (TV station, homes, school) were not specifically grid infrastructure — a distinction worth preserving rather than reading the lapse as a full ceasefire collapse.
lastChange: 2026-09-10 — 9 Sep: Russia fires Iskander-M ballistic missiles, S8000 Banderol loitering munitions, and 196 drones at Ukraine, striking a 24-story Kyiv residential building (9 injured); Ukraine strikes Russia's Novorossiysk naval base and the frigate Admiral Essen, destroys a Su-33 fighter, an Mi-8 helicopter, and two EW systems at Anapa. Neither side's 9 Sep activity specifically targeted grid infrastructure; the energy-halt question remains unresolved.
orgRelevance: Macro A&D demand context; no direct organizational action. ZNPP resolution remains relevant to critical-infrastructure-resilience monitoring.
nextIndicator: A confirmed strike specifically on Ukrainian power/grid infrastructure (would resolve the energy-halt question); any formal reciprocity confirmation; any further ZNPP power loss.

name: DoD AI Vendor Governance / Anthropic Dispute
status: DoD has rolled out custom ChatGPT and Grok instances on GenAI.mil to roughly 3 million personnel while Anthropic's Claude remains the sole major model excluded from the platform. Pentagon leadership has reaffirmed that removal of Anthropic's products from DoD systems will complete by the end of September, notwithstanding the 28 Aug district-court ruling against the underlying 'supply chain risk' designation; a second Anthropic suit remains pending before the D.C. Circuit (which previously denied a stay request).
importance: Medium — a precedent-relevant test of whether AI-vendor safety guardrails on autonomous-weapons/surveillance use cases can trigger adverse government procurement action, and whether a court ruling against such action restores market access while further litigation proceeds.
assessment: DoD is proceeding with its stated removal timeline independent of the district-court ruling and is now operationally further along (ChatGPT/Grok live, Claude absent), reinforcing that the department intends to keep litigating rather than concede the underlying dispute. The precedent remains relevant to any AI (or other) vendor navigating a similar guardrail-driven procurement dispute with a government customer.
lastChange: 2026-09-10 — no new legal filing or ruling identified this cycle; GenAI.mil rollout and month-end removal timeline both continue unchanged.
orgRelevance: Relevant to organizations assessing DoD AI-vendor stability or considering similar safety-guardrail positions in government contracting; not a direct action item absent a specific GenAI.mil dependency.
nextIndicator: D.C. Circuit ruling on Anthropic's second suit; confirmation that removal completed by month-end.
